name: Calculus for Science and Engineering I
description: Limits, continuity, derivatives of algebraic, trigonometric, and exponential functions. Mean value theorem, L'Hôpital's rule, curve sketching, optimization, and introduction to integration. First course in the calculus sequence required for DSC, CSE, and most STEM majors.

name: Calculus for Science and Engineering II
description: Techniques and applications of integration, infinite series, Taylor series, and polar coordinates. Second course in the standard calculus sequence. Prerequisite for MATH 20C and many upper-division MATH/DSC courses.

name: Calculus and Analytic Geometry for Science and Engineering
description: Multivariable calculus: vectors, partial derivatives, gradient, multiple integrals, line integrals, and vector calculus (Green's, Stokes', divergence theorems). Required prerequisite for DSC 40A, DSC 120, and DSC 123A.

name: Linear Algebra
description: Systems of linear equations, matrix operations, determinants, vector spaces, linear transformations, eigenvalues, and eigenvectors. Core mathematical foundation for nearly all upper-division DSC courses (40A, 120, 123A, 140A/B, 155).

name: Introduction to Probability
description: Sample spaces, random variables, probability distributions (discrete and continuous), expectation, variance, joint distributions, conditional probability, law of large numbers, and central limit theorem. Required or recommended for DSC 140A, 140B, 148, and 155. Prerequisite: MATH 20C.

name: Introduction to Mathematical Statistics
description: Point and interval estimation, hypothesis testing, regression, and introduction to experimental design. Provides rigorous statistical theory underlying data science methods. Prerequisite: MATH 180A.

name: Introduction to Mathematical Statistics II
description: Continuation of 181A: analysis of variance (ANOVA), nonparametric methods, multiple regression, categorical data analysis. Prerequisite: MATH 181A.

name: Statistical Methods
description: Applied statistics without the mathematical rigor of 181A: descriptive statistics, probability, hypothesis testing, regression, and ANOVA. Alternative probability/stats prerequisite accepted by several DSC upper-division courses. Prerequisite: MATH 20B.

name: Exploratory Data Analysis and Inference
description: Data exploration, visualization, statistical inference, bootstrapping, regression, and classification using real datasets and Python/R. Recommended before DSC 180A (capstone). Prerequisites: MATH 18 and MATH 180A.

name: Optimization Methods for Data Science I
description: Convexity, linear and quadratic programming, duality, support vector machines. Equivalent to DSC 123A — students may take either course to satisfy the DSC elective. Prerequisites: MATH 18 and MATH 20C.

name: Optimization Methods for Data Science II
description: Unconstrained optimization, gradient and conjugate gradient methods, ADMM. Equivalent to DSC 123B. Prerequisite: MATH 173A or DSC 123A.

name: Principal Component Analysis and Data Visualization
description: Rigorous treatment of PCA via SVD, random matrix theory, and its applications. Equivalent to DSC 155 — students may take either to satisfy the DSC elective. Prerequisites: MATH 18 and MATH 180A.

name: Principles of Data Science
description: First course in data science. Python programming with pandas, visualization, statistical inference, and prediction on real-world datasets. No prerequisites — open to all students.

name: Programming and Basic Data Structures for Data Science
description: Extends DSC 10: recursion, higher-order functions, OOP, interpreters, arrays, lists, linked lists — all in Python. Prerequisite: DSC 10.

name: Data Structures and Algorithms for Data Science
description: Advanced data structures in Java: stacks, queues, heaps, BSTs, hash tables, and algorithm complexity analysis. Multiple large programming projects. Prerequisite: DSC 20.

name: Theoretical Foundations of Data Science I
description: Mathematical ML theory: empirical risk minimization, optimization, regression, classification, and probability. Rigorous mathematical reasoning required. Prerequisites: DSC 10, MATH 20C, MATH 18.

name: Theoretical Foundations of Data Science II
description: Discrete mathematics and algorithms: runtime analysis, graph algorithms, dynamic programming, and combinatorics. Prerequisites: DSC 30 and DSC 40A.

name: The Practice and Application of Data Science
description: Hands-on data science lifecycle: EDA, data cleaning, feature engineering, and predictive modeling with pandas, NumPy, and scikit-learn on real datasets. Prerequisite: DSC 10.

name: Introduction to Data Management
description: Relational databases: ER modeling, SQL (queries, joins, aggregation, subqueries), normalization, transactions, and intro to NoSQL. Hands-on SQL projects. Prerequisites: DSC 40B and DSC 80.

name: Systems for Scalable Analytics
description: Large-scale data infrastructure: memory hierarchy, distributed systems, MapReduce/Hadoop, and Apache Spark. Covers data preparation and feature engineering at scale. Prerequisite: DSC 100.

name: Beyond Relational Data Management
description: NoSQL systems: graph databases (Neo4j), array databases, and other non-relational models. Compares expressive power of data models and covers parallel programming abstractions. Prerequisite: DSC 100.

name: Introduction to Data Visualization
description: Principles and algorithms for effective visualizations. Covers cognitive psychology, HCI, and statistical graphics; students build interactive systems using D3.js. Prerequisite: DSC 80.

name: Signal Processing for Data Analysis
description: Sampling theory, Fourier analysis, lossy compression, time/spatial filters, and wavelets applied to time series and image data. Prerequisites: MATH 18, MATH 20C, and DSC 80.

name: Optimization Methods for Data Science I
description: Convex optimization: convex sets, linear/quadratic programming, duality, support vector machines, active-set and interior-point methods. Equivalent to MATH 173A. Prerequisites: MATH 18 and MATH 20C.

name: Optimization Methods for Data Science II
description: Unconstrained optimization: gradient descent, conjugate gradient, stochastic gradient, ADMM. Equivalent to MATH 173B. Prerequisite: DSC 123A.

name: Probabilistic Modeling and Machine Learning
description: Bayesian networks, Markov models, hidden Markov models, and online learning. Applications to NLP, adversarial learning, and robotics. MATH 181A strongly recommended. Prerequisites: DSC 80 and a probability course.

name: Representation Learning
description: Deep learning fundamentals: clustering, PCA, manifold learning, MLPs, autoencoders, CNNs, and RNNs. Prerequisites: DSC 80 and a probability course.

name: Introduction to Data Mining
description: Frequent pattern mining, classification, regression, clustering, and association rules on real-world data. Cannot receive credit for both DSC 148 and CSE 158. Prerequisites: DSC 40B, DSC 80, and a probability course.

name: Hidden Data in Random Matrices
description: Rigorous PCA theory: SVD, random matrix theory (Wigner, Marchenko-Pastur, BBP transition), and community detection applications. Equivalent to MATH 182. Prerequisites: MATH 180A and MATH 18.

name: Data Science and the Arts
description: Intersection of data science and contemporary arts: authorship, representation, visualization, and data provenance. Light technical workload relative to other upper-division DSC courses. Prerequisite: DSC 80.

name: Text as Data
description: Statistical and computational text analysis for social science: tokenization, sentiment analysis, topic modeling, text classification, and word embeddings. Prerequisite: DSC 80 or equivalent.

name: Fairness and Algorithmic Decision-Making
description: Bias and fairness in algorithms: legal/ethical frameworks, auditing for discrimination, and designing equitable systems. Light workload — more reading/discussion than coding. Prerequisite: DSC 80.

name: Spatial Data Science and Applications
description: GIS, spatial big data management, geostatistics, and reasoning about location-based data. Uses GeoPandas and QGIS. Prerequisite: DSC 80.

name: Data Science Project I
description: First half of the year-long capstone. Students join faculty-led research sections, define a problem, collect/clean data, and produce a project proposal. Prerequisites: DSC 102, MATH 189, and a qualifying elective. Seniors only.

name: Data Science Project II
description: Second half of the capstone: implement the project from 180A, evaluate, and present at a public poster session. Must enroll in the section matching your 180A section. Prerequisite: DSC 180A.

name: Topics in Data Science
description: Special topics course that changes quarterly — past offerings: LLMs, causal inference, time series. May be taken four times when topic varies. Requires instructor approval. Upper-division only.

name: Seminar in Data Science
description: Invited speakers from academia and industry. Light workload — attendance and short written responses. Variable topic; may be taken three times. Prerequisite: upper-division standing.

name: Data Science Internship
description: Academic credit for a faculty-supervised research connection to your internship. Students must secure the internship independently before enrolling. Prerequisite: upper-division standing and instructor approval.

name: Directed Group Study in Data Science
description: Small-group reading and research on a faculty-proposed topic. May be taken twice. Requires department stamp and Special Studies application. Prerequisite: upper-division standing and instructor approval.

name: Independent Study for Data Science Undergraduates
description: Individual faculty-supervised research. Ideal for students considering graduate school or deepening expertise. Requires a proposal and regular faculty meetings. Prerequisite: upper-division standing and instructor approval.

name: Introduction to Programming and Computational Problem-Solving: Accelerated Pace
description: Accelerated intro to Python and Java for students with some prior programming experience. Covers OOP, data structures, algorithms, and software design. Equivalent entry to CSE 12.

name: Basic Data Structures and Object-Oriented Design
description: Java-based data structures: arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, hash tables. OOP design patterns. Accepted as an alternative to DSC 30 for some purposes. Prerequisite: CSE 11 or equivalent.

name: Software Tools and Techniques Laboratory
description: Practical Unix/Linux skills: shell scripting, version control (git), debugging tools, Vim, and Markdown. Accepted as an alternative to DSC 80 for some upper-division DSC prerequisites.

name: Advanced Data Structures
description: Balanced BSTs, heaps, tries, union-find, graph algorithms (DFS, BFS, Dijkstra), and algorithm analysis. Upper-division DS&A. Prerequisite: CSE 12.

name: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
description: Algorithm design paradigms: divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, network flow, NP-completeness, and approximation algorithms. Prerequisite: CSE 100.

name: Theoretical Foundations of Computer Science
description: Probability theory, Markov chains, information theory, and computability. Accepted as a probability alternative for some DSC upper-division prerequisites. Prerequisite: CSE 12.

name: Introduction to Machine Learning: Learning Algorithms
description: Supervised and unsupervised ML: regression, classification, neural networks, SVMs, clustering, and dimensionality reduction. Practical focus. Accepted as alternative to DSC 148/140A/140B for capstone eligibility. Prerequisites: MATH 18, probability course, and programming background.

name: Deep Learning
description: Deep neural networks in depth: CNNs, RNNs, transformers, attention mechanisms, and modern training techniques. Project-heavy course using PyTorch. Prerequisite: CSE 151A.

name: Recommender Systems and Web Mining
description: Recommendation systems, collaborative filtering, matrix factorization, and web mining. Cannot receive credit for both CSE 158 and DSC 148. Prerequisites: DSC 40B or CSE 12, DSC 80 or CSE 15L, and a probability course.

name: Linear Systems Fundamentals
description: Continuous and discrete-time signals and systems, convolution, Fourier transform, Laplace transform, z-transform, sampling theorem, and filter design. Prerequisite: MATH 20C.

name: Engineering Probability and Statistics
description: Probability, random variables, distributions, expectation, and intro to random processes. Widely accepted as an alternative to MATH 180A for DSC upper-division prerequisites. Prerequisite: MATH 20C.

name: Data Science in Practice
description: Applied data science using Python: data collection, wrangling, analysis, visualization, and communication of findings. Team-based project course emphasizing the full data science workflow. Prerequisite: a programming course.

name: Introduction to Machine Learning
description: Supervised and unsupervised ML methods: regression, classification, neural networks, and evaluation. Accepted as a qualifying ML elective for DSC 180A capstone eligibility. Prerequisites: MATH 18, a probability course, and programming background.

name: Physics — Mechanics
description: Kinematics, Newton's laws, work and energy, momentum, rotational motion, gravitation, and oscillations. First course in the non-calculus physics sequence. Prerequisite: MATH 20B (concurrent OK).

name: Physics — Electricity and Magnetism
description: Electrostatics, circuits, magnetism, Maxwell's equations, and electromagnetic waves. Prerequisite: PHYS 2A and MATH 20C (concurrent OK).

name: Physics — Waves, Optics, and Modern Physics
description: Waves, optics, special relativity, quantum mechanics intro, and atomic/nuclear physics. Third course in the non-calculus sequence. Prerequisite: PHYS 2B.

name: Physics for Physics Majors — Mechanics
description: Rigorous mechanics for physics majors: Newton's laws, energy, momentum, rotation, oscillations, and gravitation using calculus throughout. Prerequisite: MATH 20C (concurrent OK).

name: Physics for Physics Majors — Electricity and Magnetism
description: Electrostatics, Gauss's law, circuits, magnetic forces, Faraday's law, and Maxwell's equations with calculus. Prerequisite: PHYS 4A.

name: Physics for Physics Majors — Waves, Optics, and Modern Physics
description: Wave mechanics, optics, special relativity, and intro to quantum mechanics. Prerequisite: PHYS 4B.

name: General Chemistry I
description: Atomic theory, bonding, stoichiometry, thermochemistry, and gas laws. First course in the general chemistry sequence. Prerequisites: high school chemistry or CHEM 4.

name: General Chemistry II
description: Chemical equilibrium, acid-base chemistry, electrochemistry, kinetics, and intro to nuclear chemistry. Prerequisite: CHEM 6A.

name: General Chemistry III
description: Thermodynamics, coordination chemistry, organic chemistry introduction, and biological molecules. Completes the general chemistry sequence. Prerequisite: CHEM 6B.

name: The Periodic Table
description: Single-quarter survey of general chemistry: atomic structure, bonding, reactions, stoichiometry, and molecular properties. Alternative to 6A for students who need only one chemistry course. No prerequisites.

name: The Cell
description: Cell structure, biochemistry, metabolism, cell division, genetics, and intro to molecular biology. Foundation course for all BIOL sequences. No prerequisites.

name: Multicellular Life
description: Development, physiology, and body systems of multicellular organisms. Second course in the BILD foundation sequence. Prerequisite: BILD 1.

name: Organismic and Evolutionary Biology
description: Evolution, ecology, population genetics, and diversity of life. Third course in the BILD sequence. Prerequisite: BILD 1.

name: Structural Biochemistry
description: Protein structure and function, enzymes, membranes, and metabolic pathways. Core biochemistry course. Prerequisites: CHEM 6C or 6BH, and BILD 1.

name: Metabolic Biochemistry
description: Central metabolic pathways: glycolysis, TCA cycle, oxidative phosphorylation, fatty acid metabolism, and amino acid metabolism. Prerequisite: BIBC 100.
